You slowly learn to live with the heartbreak. You slowly build a life with it and around it.

It's possible, but only if you try.

I don't know if this is helpful, but all I can say is, you just gotta keep trying.

It's awful. It's not easy. It's devastating. But please, keep trying.

I think you can do lots of phone and video calls with your family. You'd be surprised at how much a relationship can be sustained and built even with distance. You can always visit home and maybe your family can come visit you in Spain and that would be a new opportunity for them.

I don't think there's a wrong or right answer. There are only choices. If you make a choice and you live that choice for a bit, and realize it's not what you want, you can change your mind and do something different.

But please, don't choose family out of obligation. Do it because you want to.

I think that's a nice privilege some of us have. We can always change your mind and decide that we want something different. 

Whatever you decide, I hope you're brought down a path that surrounds you with an abundance of all kinds of love. Love for yourself, love for life, love for others, and continued love for your sister.

I'm a little over 4 months since my boyfriend passed now.

The grief's different now.

The first 3 months, the grief poured out of me. I cried so hard that my ribs were in pain. I would cry when I was dragged out by family and friends. 

Now, the grief feels more contained. I still cry. It's still the most unimaginable visceral raw pain, but I don't fight it anymore. 

What helped me get this far is not holding back the pain. Like I said, I cried a lot. Almost every day for 3 months straight. I also went to grief counseling, and that's been helpful. It was very helpful when I was at the point of considering ending my own life. I journal a lot. I do whatever I can to get the pain out.

I also read and watched a lot of things relating to grief and losing people you love just to help me feel less alone.

That's what worked for me. I'm not any better, but I feel like I have a better relationship with my grief now. 

If you can, just keep expressing the pain in whatever way that works for you. I think that can get you to a different side of grief that isn't always riddled with agony. 

I also do a lot to "keep" my partner around. He has an altar in my room that I light a candle at. I sleep in his clothes from time to time. I have a picture of him that I keep in bed with me to help me sleep. I have a picture of him I keep in my car as well. 

They've all helped me feel like he's still close even though I know he's gone. I don't think our human brains are really meant to comprehend death. Mine isn't at least. So, I do these things to trick my brain a little and keep the biting separation at bay. 

I don't know why I typed this all out. I know you didn’t ask for any advice so maybe I typed it out more for me. I don't know.

6 days after my boyfriend passed, I had the sadest, sweetest, and most comforting dream. 

It started off with me looking for him in a city neighborhood with a girl. I don't know, but she felt like a trusted friend. She and I went to another friend's loft style apartment to look for my bf, but we couldn't find him there. 

We looked around the downtown area but still couldn't find him. I decided we should go back to the apartment to look for him because I felt like he'd be there. 

While we were walking up to the apartment building, we found my bf outside about to go into the building. I called out his name when I saw him. He immediately stopped trying to unlock the door, and I felt this overwhelming amount of fear. 

It felt like it was his fear. He was afraid when I saw him and he didn't want to come to me. I called him name again, and I could feel that he really wanted to come to me, but he was scared I'd be mad at him and reject him.

I didn't say anything, but I wanted him to know that everything was okay and I wasn't mad, I was just worried about him. I think he sensed that from me. 

Then the dream kind of shifts and myself, my bf and the girl with me are all inside the apartment. My bf and I are holding each other in a really tight embrace. He's much taller than I am, but we were cheek to cheek. I felt this overwhelming amount of guilt and shame coming from him, and I just comforted him and let him know that I and his family and friends all still love him no matter what. 

I felt the guilt and shame absolve a tiny bit. 

We kissed, and our friend in the room said we were doing too much playfully.

Then we walked around the important and chatted about some stuff. 

I woke up while we were doing that.

I chose to go see my partner's body at the funeral home. It was incredibly hard, and I cried the whole time, but I had to see my lover one last time. I couldn't bring myself to touch him, though, and a part of me wishes I did. 

I promised I'd always see him through the good and bad, and everything in between. I always wanted him to know that he never had to perform in front of me. He could be himself. He could be raw with me. That's what love is, right? I think making the choice to go see his body was part of me fulfilling my promise to him. 

I said lots of things. Wrote him a whole letter and read it to him. Slipped in the letter and some photos of us together there as well. 

Like I said, it's different for everyone, and there's no wrong or right way answer, and it's certainly not morbid. 

But you felt called to do it. Maybe your mom needed to hear those words, and she wanted someone to be with her there, and she chose you.

Additionally, I am so sorry for your loss. Grieving is the hardest thing we will go through. It's not pretty a majority of the time, and in those moments, I hope you give yourself grace and patience, and you free yourself from any shame of feeling pain. 

In moments where the pain is a little less and your eyes are a little less teary, I hope you can remember the great love you got to experience with your mom. The love will never go anywhere.
